title: Modularize routing policy and migrate fallback state to lock-free queue
creator: Maya Patel
description: Refactor the smart routing layer to a modular plugin model and replace the global synchronized fallback state with a lock-free, single-producer single-consumer queue. This reduces hotpath contention, simplifies adding new policy adapters (region affinity, cost-based routing, tenant overrides), and prepares the codebase for an upcoming dependency upgrade of the eventbus and protocol buffer runtime. The goal is to reduce router p95 latency and CPU tail usage under heavy bursts while enabling safer rollout of new policy adapters.
acceptance_criteria: Router unit tests and integration tests green in CI (no behavior regressions)
Canary rollout to 10% of traffic with automatic rollback on error rate > 0.5% or latency regression > 10%
Observed p95 request routing latency improvement >= 10% in synthetic burst tests
CPU steal/contention metrics on router processes reduced vs baseline during soak tests
New plugin adapter interface documented and an example adapter (region-weighted) merged
Eventbus and protobuf minor upgrades integrated and verified with no API breakage
implementation_plan: 1) Extract PolicyAdapter interface and move existing policy implementations behind it (region, cost, tier). Add adapter registry and loader with feature-flagged activation.
2) Introduce LockFreeFallbackQueue implementing existing fallback semantics; wire it behind a feature flag and shadow-read fallback decisions for 1 week.
3) Replace global synchronized fallback map usages on the hot path with lightweight read-only accessors that consult the lock-free queue snapshot.
4) Upgrade eventbus library to v2.1 and protobuf runtime to 3.20.x; fix generated bindings and rebuild CI images.
5) Add integration tests that simulate regional failover and capacity pressure; run soak for 24 hours in staging with traffic replay.
6) Canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated checks; plan rollback steps and postmortem template prepared.
7) Post-rollout: remove legacy synchronized fallback code paths and land cleanup PRs within 2 weeks.
Estimated timeline: 3 weeks active work + 2 weeks staging soak and rollouts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: subtle behavior change in fallback ordering could increase error rates. Mitigation: shadow mode for 1 week comparing old vs new decisions, produce diff logs for a sampling of requests.
Risk: eventbus/protobuf upgrade causes serialization incompatibility. Mitigation: add compatibility checks in CI, keep serialization versioning shim available for rollback.
Risk: lock-free queue introduces memory growth in pathological sequences. Mitigation: bounded queue with backpressure metric and circuit breaker to fall back to legacy path if thresholds exceeded.
Risk: plugin registry misconfiguration leads to dropped policies. Mitigation: safe defaults and require explicit opt-in for experimental adapters via config; validate config at startup.
Risk: rollout increases tail latency under specific traffic mixes. Mitigation: staged canary with targeted traffic shapes and pre-defined rollback thresholds.
testing_plan: Unit tests for PolicyAdapter contract and fallback queue invariants (durability, boundedness, ordering)
Integration tests: region failover scenarios, capacity-constrained routing, and multi-tenant fairness checks
Load tests: synthetic bursts to recreate prior hotpath contention; compare p95/p99 latency and CPU utilization
Shadow-run in staging for one week to capture discrepancy logs and edge-case routing decisions
Canary with telemetry dashboards: latency, error-rate, fallback-count, queue-depth, memory growth
notes: Design review 2025-02-14: agreed on adapter registry and explicit opt-in for experimental adapters.
Security notes: bumping protobuf required re-running our schema linter; KMS paths unaffected but signed payloads were tested.
We decided to use a bounded MPMC-friendly ring buffer with single consumer for the hotpath to minimise CAS storms.
Implementation initially attempted a lock-striping map; abandoned due to complexity and suboptimal p99 under bursts.
